data.content_ref: inline:The target claims to defend Popper's preference for *better-corroborated* theories without induction, but the mechanism silently substitutes a different selection criterion — *highest empirical content among unfalsified theories* — thereby failing to defend the very preference named in the claim. Corroboration is a track-record property (a theory has survived severe tests), whereas empirical content is an a priori property (how many possible observations the theory rules out). A newly conjectured theory can have the highest empirical content of any unfalsified competitor yet have zero corroboration because it has never been tested. Popper's actual preference is for the better-corroborated theory, which necessarily weighs past testing success. By redefining the criterion as 'most informative surviving conjecture for further testing' and then equating that with 'highest empirical content that has not yet been falsified,' the mechanism avoids the induction problem only by abandoning corroboration — the very notion Popper's preference is built on — and replacing it with a content-maximality rule that Popper never endorsed. If the original criterion (better-corroborated) is reinstated, the defense collapses, because preferring a theory on the basis of its past testing record is precisely the inductive inference the target promised to avoid.
